caption: Everyone assumes a doctor's salary is sorted. Is R3 800 left over enough to call that comfortable?

slides.title:
How I spend my
R38 400 p/m as a
community service doctor
South Africa
Living in Pinetown
slides.body:
Male, 29
Single, no kids
Job: Community service doctor, provincial hospital
Net salary: R38 400 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 1 bed in Westville, close to the highway
slides.body: I pay this so I can sleep in silence after a 30 hour call.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My parents' bond contribution, my sister's university fees
slides.body: They paid for my degree. This line isn't a favour, it's the other half of the deal.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: I bought it in my fifth year because the bus stopped feeling safe.

slides.title: Study loan
slides.includes: Repayment on the loan that covered what the bursary didn't
slides.body: Six years of loan and I'm only now paying more than the interest.

slides.title: Eating out
slides.includes: Takeaways between shifts, one decent dinner a month
slides.body: I'm a doctor. I know what I'm eating. I eat it anyway.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Groceries, petrol, medical aid, phone, HPCSA registration, indemnity, funeral policy, gym
slides.body: The registration fee is a yearly shock I've spread across the months.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R38 400. Looks comfortable, until you add that I'm responsible for three households.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I put my statement into Beyond Horizon and the study loan and parent contributions sat next to my own spending for the first time.

The takeaway number was the awkward one.

No bank login needed.
